description_full: Bank Polska Kasa Opieki S.A., a commercial bank, provides banking products and services to retail and corporate clients in Poland. It operates through Retail Banking and Private Banking; Enterprise banking; and Corporate and Investment Banking segments. The company offers bank accounts, deposits and certificates of deposit, payment cards, loan products, mortgage and consumer loans, and insurance products. It is also involved in the brokering activity and sale of investment products; leasing, factoring, arranging issues of debt securities, and other specialized forms of financing; and transactional banking. In addition, the company provides investment advisory services, advisory in M&A, advanced treasury, capital market products, and custody services; investment banking; structured finance; financing of commercial real estate projects, including financing of the construction of warehouses; and other services, such as collecting information on debtors' financial situation, collection, debt collection, settlements accounting, and monitoring of payments. Further, it is involved in the settlement of mass transactions, financial advisory and consulting services regarding the selection of financing method, and granting loans and credits related to the factoring agreement; brokerage services for large and medium-sized enterprises and financial institutions; payment card management systems, transaction authorization and card personalization; online payment systems; and financial intermediation and transfer agent services. Bank Polska Kasa Opieki S.A. was founded in 1929 and is headquartered in Warsaw, Poland.

financial_summary: BANK POLSKA KASA OPIEKI SA is a large-cap financial services business with a $18.2B market cap on $4.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +22% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

The business throws off $2.1B in free cash flow — roughly 48 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.32× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 25.3× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss.

Management returns a meaningful 6.7% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 20% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
